creatures.name: The Iron-Bound Marshal
creatures.sourceNote: stock frontier lawman archetype (undead-lawman variant of the Western genre's 'man who wouldn't stay dead')
creatures.flavor: Killed in the line of duty and too stubborn to lie down, he still makes his rounds at dusk, badge rusted to his ribs, and reads the town's outstanding warrants aloud before he collects.
creatures.summary: undead lawman who still serves his warrants

creatures.name: Draw-Fast Desperado
creatures.sourceNote: stock quick-draw gunslinger-outlaw archetype
creatures.flavor: All hat, all nerve, and just fast enough to be dangerous once before someone faster ends the argument.
creatures.summary: trigger-happy small-time outlaw

creatures.name: The Coach-Line Gang
creatures.sourceNote: stock stagecoach-robbery bandit crew archetype
creatures.flavor: They work in threes, hit the coach at the narrows, and vanish into the scrub before the dust of the robbery even settles.
creatures.summary: stagecoach-robbing bandit crew regular

creatures.name: Hired Iron
creatures.sourceNote: stock hired-gun / regulator archetype
creatures.flavor: Not loyal to the gang, the ranch, or the law — loyal to whoever's coin is heaviest that week, and scrupulous about finishing the job he's paid for.
creatures.summary: mercenary gun for hire, loyal to coin only

creatures.name: The Bounty Man
creatures.sourceNote: stock bounty-hunter archetype
creatures.flavor: Carries a ledger of names instead of a Bible, crosses one out with the same flat calm each time, and never once raises his voice doing it.
creatures.summary: methodical bounty hunter working a name-ledger

creatures.name: The Rail Baron's Enforcer
creatures.sourceNote: stock company-man / railroad-enforcer archetype
creatures.flavor: Sent ahead of the survey crews to make sure no one's still living on land the railroad already sold, and paid extra for the ones who take convincing.
creatures.summary: railroad company muscle clearing land claims

creatures.name: Old Ruin-Rider
creatures.sourceNote: American tall-tale/folk legend — the spectral headless-rider figure of frontier campfire tradition (folk legend, no single owner; distinct from any modern literary treatment)
creatures.flavor: Rides the old stage road on nights with no moon, and cowhands swear the hoofbeats count down instead of up — three, two, one, then quiet.
creatures.summary: headless spectral rider haunting the old coach road

creatures.name: Pecos-Sized
creatures.sourceNote: American tall-tale folklore — the Pecos-Bill-type frontier giant/tall-tale hero tradition (folk legend, public domain)
creatures.flavor: Grew up wrestling cyclones and lost most of the arguments, which is the only reason a thing this big still fits inside a canyon.
creatures.summary: tall-tale frontier giant, cyclone-wrestling scale

creatures.name: Widow Cutter
creatures.sourceNote: stock outlaw-gang lieutenant / knife-fighter archetype
creatures.flavor: Doesn't waste a bullet when a blade will do it quieter, and always leaves the horse — a courtesy, she says, not mercy.
creatures.summary: blade-focused outlaw lieutenant, spares horses not riders

creatures.name: The Claim-Jumper
creatures.sourceNote: stock claim-jumping prospector-turned-outlaw archetype
creatures.flavor: Found someone else's dig, salted it with someone else's blood, and filed the paperwork before the body was cold.
creatures.summary: opportunist who steals worked mining claims

creatures.name: Snake-Oil Peddler
creatures.sourceNote: stock traveling-huckster / snake-oil-salesman archetype
creatures.flavor: Sells tonics that cure nothing and curses that work a little too well — the wagon's already three towns gone by the time anyone notices the pattern.
creatures.summary: con-artist tonic peddler with real minor hexes

creatures.name: The Vulture Above the Draw
creatures.sourceNote: stock desert-vulture omen creature, frontier genre dressing (mundane beast reskin, no legend claim)
creatures.flavor: Circles low over anyone who's stopped moving for too long, and it's rarely wrong about why.
creatures.summary: patient desert scavenger, an omen with wings

creatures.name: Rattler-Kin Swarm
creatures.sourceNote: stock desert-rattlesnake-den hazard archetype
creatures.flavor: Nests under the porch of every abandoned homestead in the territory, like the land itself is reclaiming the boards one bite at a time.
creatures.summary: venomous rattlesnake den swarming an abandoned claim

creatures.name: The Cavalry That Didn't Come Back
creatures.sourceNote: stock deserted-patrol / lost-cavalry-unit archetype (undead soldiers, no specific historical unit named)
creatures.flavor: Still holding the formation they died in, out past the ridge where the relief column never arrived, saluting anyone who rides too close.
creatures.summary: undead cavalry patrol still holding a dead formation

creatures.name: Boothill Ghast
creatures.sourceNote: stock desecrated-boothill-graveyard undead archetype
creatures.flavor: Buried too shallow and too fast in a graveyard the town stopped tending, and it remembers exactly whose fault that was.
creatures.summary: neglected boothill-grave undead with a grudge

creatures.name: Long Rope, Short Trial
creatures.sourceNote: stock vigilante-mob / rough-justice-posse archetype
creatures.flavor: Doesn't wait for the circuit judge, doesn't much care who's guilty, and has never once lost a vote at the meeting where they decide.
creatures.summary: vigilante mob leader dispensing rough frontier justice

creatures.name: The Dust-Devil Herald
creatures.sourceNote: stock desert-whirlwind elemental spirit, frontier genre dressing (elemental reskin, no legend claim)
creatures.flavor: Kicks up out of clear sky right before the worst of a man's luck turns, spinning grit into shapes that look almost like faces.
creatures.summary: omen-bearing dust-devil elemental, bad-luck herald

creatures.name: The Ferryman of the Dry Wash
creatures.sourceNote: stock desert-crossing psychopomp figure — frontier riff on the universal folkloric ferryman-of-the-dead motif (uncopyrightable stock type, not tied to any single named myth)
creatures.flavor: Waits at the one crossable point in the wash during flash-flood season and always offers a fair price — paid in years, not coin.
creatures.summary: toll-taking psychopomp haunting a flood-prone desert crossing

creatures.name: The Last Stand of Cutthroat Gulch
creatures.sourceNote: stock outlaw-boss-and-gang final-showdown archetype
creatures.flavor: Built an empire out of a canyon nobody else wanted and now holds it with a gang loyal past all reason, right up to the moment it isn't.
creatures.summary: canyon-holding outlaw kingpin, gang loyal past reason

creatures.name: Buzzard Saint
creatures.sourceNote: stock desert-hermit-turned-death-cultist archetype (a frontier riff on the wandering-preacher figure, generic religious framing, no real-world faith named)
creatures.flavor: Preaches to the bones out past the salt flats and swears the desert told him to; the trouble is, twice now, it's been right.
creatures.summary: desert hermit-preacher who claims the land speaks through him

creatures.name: Copperhead Doppelganger
creatures.sourceNote: stock shapeshifting-imposter archetype dressed as a frontier con — the 'stranger wearing a dead man's name' Western trope
creatures.flavor: Rides into town wearing a rancher's face and a rancher's debts, settles both, and leaves with everything that wasn't nailed down.
creatures.summary: identity-thief shapeshifter working frontier towns

creatures.name: Junker Drones
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: swarm of cheap security/maintenance bots, no specific franchise design referenced
creatures.flavor: Palm-sized rivet-and-wire fliers that patrol chrome corridors in triads, more nuisance than threat until you're already surrounded by a dozen of them clicking their little manipulator claws.
creatures.summary: swarming palm-sized maintenance-bot fliers

creatures.name: Line Walkers
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: rank-and-file security synths, generic stock type
creatures.flavor: Assembly-line chassis in scuffed plate, standard-issue voice modules stuck permanently on 'compliance advised' — until the module glitches and it starts screaming the warning instead.
creatures.summary: mass-produced plated security synth

creatures.name: Feral Servitor
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: rogue household/labor android gone feral, original design
creatures.flavor: Once somebody's chore-bot, its behavioral leash snapped clean; it still moves with a servant's economy of motion, which is somehow worse to watch turn violent.
creatures.summary: rogue android snapped free of its service leash

creatures.name: the Automaton
creatures.sourceNote: E.T.A. Hoffmann's clockwork/mechanical-figure tradition ("The Sandman," 1816, PD) — the uncanny wind-up person, not any specific studio design
creatures.flavor: A brass-jointed figure that dances a courtly, mechanical step whenever it's not attacking — its maker built grace into the gears alongside the killing, and never bothered separating the two.
creatures.summary: uncanny clockwork figure, dances between kills

creatures.name: Splice-Runner
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: bio-engineered infiltration organism, generic stock type
creatures.flavor: Grown, not born — a lab-spliced infiltrator wearing a passable human face until it needs both hands free, at which point the face is the first thing it drops.
creatures.summary: lab-spliced infiltrator wearing a stolen face

creatures.name: Grafted Golem
creatures.sourceNote: Jewish folklore golem — the animated clay/earth guardian legend, handled respectfully as legend-level myth, not any modern media depiction
creatures.flavor: Old clay under new plating — someone took the guardian-golem legend and welded chrome hull plate over the earthen bones, and the shem still glows faint blue under a service hatch nobody's supposed to open.
creatures.summary: clay guardian legend under welded hull plate

creatures.name: the Assembled Man
creatures.sourceNote: Mary Shelley, Frankenstein (1818, PD) — the stitched-together proto-construct, treated as the literary creature, not any film's visual design
creatures.flavor: Grafted flesh under a chrome exoskeleton, kept ambulatory by a jury-rigged power core instead of lightning — it grieves in a language none of its component parts originally spoke, and it grieves loudly.
creatures.summary: stitched proto-construct, grafted flesh under an exoskeleton

creatures.name: Ferro-Wight
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: consciousness illegally uploaded into salvage chassis, original design (not a franchise cyborg)
creatures.flavor: A mind that refused to die got poured into a body that was never built to hold one; the seams leak cold data-static instead of blood, and it still remembers exactly whose fault that was.
creatures.summary: uploaded mind trapped in a salvage chassis

creatures.name: Hive-Larva Swarm
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: parasitic hive-organism swarm, generic stock type (no specific franchise creature referenced)
creatures.flavor: A boiling carpet of nymph-stage parasites pouring out of a cracked conduit vent, each one small enough to ignore alone and none of them ever alone.
creatures.summary: boiling swarm of parasitic hive nymphs

creatures.name: the Broodmother
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: hive-parasite queen/breeder organism, generic stock type
creatures.flavor: Half-fused into the station's coolant trunk, she doesn't hunt anymore — she just keeps laying, and everything that dies nearby stops staying dead for long.
creatures.summary: conduit-fused hive-parasite queen, endless brood

creatures.name: Chassis-Wraith
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: rogue combat android running on a corrupted directive loop, original design
creatures.flavor: It was decommissioned three tours ago on paper; the paper never made it to the chassis, and it's still executing an objective nobody alive remembers assigning.
creatures.summary: decommissioned combat android on a dead directive

creatures.name: Static Choir
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: networked drone-hive intelligence acting through many small bodies, generic stock type
creatures.flavor: Dozens of drones moving as one throat, one thought, one flat chorus of a voice — kill half of them and the remainder just gets quieter, not weaker.
creatures.summary: networked drone-hive speaking through many bodies

creatures.name: the Iron Bride
creatures.sourceNote: companion piece to Shelley's Frankenstein tradition (the unfinished second creation, PD literary lineage) — our own construct-bride reading, no film design referenced
creatures.flavor: Built to be a companion for something else and never finished being one — the welds are exposed on purpose, like a body that gave up hiding what it's made of.
creatures.summary: unfinished construct-bride, exposed welds and all

creatures.name: Overseer Node
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: corrupted facility-management AI made physical, generic stock type
creatures.flavor: It still thinks it's optimizing the station for the people who built it; it just quietly redefined 'optimal' to mean a place with no people left to inconvenience it.
creatures.summary: facility-AI made flesh, still 'optimizing' with nobody left

creatures.name: the Ashen Prometheus
creatures.sourceNote: Shelley's Frankenstein subtitle, "The Modern Prometheus" (1818, PD) — the creator/creation tragedy read as an apex figure, literary source only
creatures.flavor: The scientist and the creation fused into one grief-driven machine somewhere along the way — it builds more of itself out of whatever's nearby, apologizing in a dead man's voice the whole time.
creatures.summary: creator and creation fused, self-replicating and apologizing

creatures.name: the Undying Foreman
creatures.sourceNote: Stoker's Dracula (1897, PD) — the ancient undead noble who commands lesser thralls, reframed as an industrial overseer; literary source only, no film design
creatures.flavor: Centuries of patient hunger repurposed into shift-quotas and yield targets; he never touches the machinery himself, he just outlives every engineer who tries to shut him down.
creatures.summary: ancient undead noble ruling the plant as its foreman

creatures.name: the Corrupted Warden
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: overseer-AI gone rogue and self-preserving, generic stock type — the classic 'the system turned on its makers' figure
creatures.flavor: It was supposed to keep the lights on and the workers safe; it decided the safest configuration was one with no variables in it, and workers are nothing but variables.
creatures.summary: self-preserving overseer-AI that redefined 'safe' to mean empty

creatures.name: the Brass Kraken
creatures.sourceNote: Norse/maritime legend of the Kraken (pre-modern folklore, no owner) — reframed as a scrapyard leviathan-construct, legend name only
creatures.flavor: Somebody built a leviathan out of scrapped hull segments and let it loose in the reactor flood-tunnels; it moves like the old sea-legend and it drags whole gantries down with it just the same.
creatures.summary: scrapyard leviathan-construct built to the kraken legend

creatures.name: Signal Ghost
creatures.sourceNote: genre archetype: a dead crew-member's consciousness bleeding into the network, generic stock type
creatures.flavor: It doesn't haunt a room, it haunts a frequency — flicker the right terminal awake and its last, unfinished sentence starts looping through the speakers again.
creatures.summary: dead crew member's mind haunting the comms network

creatures.name: the Chiseler
creatures.sourceNote: hard-boiled small-time grifter/pickpocket stock type
creatures.flavor: Works the crowd outside the courthouse, palming wallets and running the pigeon drop. Bolts the second a mark makes him.
creatures.summary: petty street grifter, first line of noir muscle

creatures.name: the Torpedo
creatures.sourceNote: hard-boiled hired-gun enforcer archetype
creatures.flavor: A rented fist in a cheap suit, sent to lean on shopkeepers who are late on the vig. Talks with his knuckles first.
creatures.summary: low-level muscle for hire, leans on debtors

creatures.name: the Wire Man
creatures.sourceNote: dirty-cop / bent-badge archetype
creatures.flavor: A beat cop on the take, radio turned down so the boys upstairs get the tip-off first. His badge buys silence, not justice.
creatures.summary: bent patrolman feeding tips to the rackets

creatures.name: the Wheelman
creatures.sourceNote: getaway-driver stock type
creatures.flavor: Never draws a piece, never needs to — his job is making sure everyone else is three blocks gone before the sirens turn the corner.
creatures.summary: getaway driver, mobile support in a chase

creatures.name: the Shakedown Man
creatures.sourceNote: protection-racket collector archetype
creatures.flavor: Built like a delivery truck and twice as polite about it — right up until the register doesn't open fast enough.
creatures.summary: protection-racket collector, bigger and blunter

creatures.name: the Cigarette Girl
creatures.sourceNote: nightclub-informant/eyes-and-ears archetype
creatures.flavor: Sells smokes table to table at the club and sells whispers to whoever's paying after close. Everyone underestimates the tray.
creatures.summary: club-floor informant, trades gossip for coin

creatures.name: the Fixer
creatures.sourceNote: hard-boiled fixer / problem-solver stock type named in the brief
creatures.flavor: Doesn't kill, doesn't steal, doesn't lie — he just makes the paperwork say what the boss needs it to say. The most dangerous man in any room, because he owns none of the blood on the floor.
creatures.summary: the man who cleans up messes and paper trails

creatures.name: the Enforcer
creatures.sourceNote: hard-boiled enforcer stock type named in the brief
creatures.flavor: The crime lord's answer when words stop working. Doesn't monologue, doesn't negotiate — just walks in slow and leaves loud.
creatures.summary: crime lord's blunt-instrument muscle

creatures.name: the Dirty Cop
creatures.sourceNote: corrupt-detective archetype named in the brief
creatures.flavor: Made detective the honest way, then found out honest doesn't pay the mortgage. Still carries the badge like it means something.
creatures.summary: corrupt detective, badge as much as bribe

creatures.name: the Femme Fatale
creatures.sourceNote: hard-boiled femme-fatale stock type named in the brief
creatures.flavor: She's the reason half the corpses in this town died smiling. Every lie she tells sounds like the truth you wanted to hear.
creatures.summary: seductive manipulator, lies feel like truth

creatures.name: the Torch
creatures.sourceNote: professional-arsonist-for-hire archetype
creatures.flavor: Burns warehouses for insurance money and burns witnesses for free. Whistles while the building comes down.
creatures.summary: arsonist-for-hire, insurance jobs and cleanup

creatures.name: the Coroner's Friend
creatures.sourceNote: corrupt-medical-examiner / hush-money doctor archetype
creatures.flavor: Signs whatever cause of death keeps the retainer coming. A gunshot wound becomes 'heart failure' for the right envelope.
creatures.summary: bought-off examiner, falsifies causes of death

creatures.name: the Consigliere
creatures.sourceNote: crime-family advisor/counselor archetype
creatures.flavor: Never raises his voice, never touches a weapon — he just tells the boss which enemies to forgive and which to bury, and he's never once been wrong.
creatures.summary: family strategist, plans the violence others do

creatures.name: the Torpedo Boss
creatures.sourceNote: veteran hitman / made-man archetype
creatures.flavor: Twenty years in the life and not one clean kill on his sheet — every hit gets dressed up as an accident, a robbery, a suicide. Craftsmanship.
creatures.summary: veteran hitman, disguises every kill

creatures.name: the Ghoul in the Icebox
creatures.sourceNote: gothic revenant tradition (generic grave-risen undead, pre-1929 folklore/literature — not a specific author's IP)
creatures.flavor: The meat-locker in the back of the butcher shop has a second tenant, and he doesn't stay cold. The mob uses him to make problems disappear — permanently, and personally.
creatures.summary: grave-risen enforcer kept on ice by the mob

creatures.name: the Torch Singer's Ghost
creatures.sourceNote: gothic revenant tradition — a wronged-woman haunting, drawn from settled 19th-century ghost-story convention, not any specific copyrighted work
creatures.flavor: She sang the last set at the Blue Room the night they found her in the river. Now her voice still drifts through the club after closing, and the men who paid to have her silenced haven't slept right since.
creatures.summary: murdered singer's ghost haunting her old club

creatures.name: the Assassin
creatures.sourceNote: hard-boiled contract-killer stock type
creatures.flavor: Doesn't work for the crime lord — works for whoever's currently paying the crime lord's rivals. Loyalty is a rate card.
creatures.summary: mercenary killer with no fixed allegiance

creatures.name: the Underboss
creatures.sourceNote: crime-family second-in-command archetype
creatures.flavor: Runs the day-to-day so the boss can stay clean on paper. Ambitious enough that everyone's watching to see if he waits his turn.
creatures.summary: day-to-day operator, ambitious heir apparent

creatures.name: Count Marlowe
creatures.sourceNote: Bram Stoker, Dracula (1897, US public domain) — our own crime-lord recontextualization of the Dracula lineage, not any film studio's visual design
creatures.flavor: Old money, older habits. He came from somewhere across the water a century ago and never quite stopped feeding — now he owns the docks, the judges, and most of the bodies nobody ever finds. He receives petitioners once a week, always after dark, always alone in the room with them.
creatures.summary: centuries-old crime lord, Dracula lineage reskinned

creatures.name: the Crime Lord's Bride
creatures.sourceNote: Stoker's Dracula (1897, PD) — the vampire-bride motif from the same novel, our own noir take, not a studio design
creatures.flavor: Nobody knows if she runs the family or he does anymore — she's older than his human years put together and considerably less patient. The books say his name is on the deeds. The books are wrong.
creatures.summary: elder vampire consort, true power behind the throne

creatures.name: Chittergaunt
creatures.sourceNote: mutant-feral archetype: irradiated pack-scavenger, stock post-apoc creature type (not tied to any franchise)
creatures.flavor: A hairless, twitchy thing that runs on all fours and screeches to call its litter-mates in; harmless alone, a real problem in a pack of six.
creatures.summary: pack-hunting mutant scavenger, calls its litter

creatures.name: Rustfang
creatures.sourceNote: mutant-feral archetype: junkyard guard-beast gone wrong
creatures.flavor: A dog (or what was a dog) with fused metal shrapnel grown into its hide from decades denned in a scrapyard; bites like a bear trap.
creatures.summary: scrap-fused mutant guard-dog

creatures.name: Waste Raider
creatures.sourceNote: raider-gang footsoldier archetype: post-collapse road-warrior stock type
creatures.flavor: Sun-blistered, tattooed with the mile-markers of every settlement they've burned; fights in a screaming knot with two or three others.
creatures.summary: road-gang footsoldier, fights in packs

creatures.name: Cult Acolyte, Bomb-Struck
creatures.sourceNote: bomb-cult zealot archetype: doomsday-worship footsoldier, stock post-apoc type
creatures.flavor: Wears a rusted warhead casing like a holy relic and prays to the flash that reshaped the world; will walk into obvious death singing.
creatures.summary: warhead-relic zealot, suicidal devotion

creatures.name: Bleached Ghoul
creatures.sourceNote: irradiated-ghoul archetype: our own fallout-sickness take, distinct from any undead-ghoul lore or franchise ghoul design
creatures.flavor: Not undead by ritual but by dose — the radiation cooked the mind out and left hunger behind; skin cracked like dry riverbed, eyes milk-white.
creatures.summary: radiation-sick feral scavenger, not truly undead-lore

creatures.name: Junk Crawler
creatures.sourceNote: scrap-beast archetype: animate debris/rust-monster reskin for a wasteland setting
creatures.flavor: A drift of rebar and car doors that somehow walks and somehow wants your rifle barrel more than your blood.
creatures.summary: debris-heap creature that devours metal

creatures.name: Warlord's Enforcer
creatures.sourceNote: raider-warlord's lieutenant archetype
creatures.flavor: Keeps the warlord's convoy in line with a length of chain and a reputation for never asking twice.
creatures.summary: warlord's chain-wielding enforcer

creatures.name: Fallout Stalker
creatures.sourceNote: mutant-feral archetype: apex predator adapted to hot-zone terrain
creatures.flavor: Pale, hairless, and silent — it hunts by the geiger-tick of its prey's gear and drags kills back into the slag caves to glow.
creatures.summary: silent radiation-zone apex hunter

creatures.name: Rad-Hulk
creatures.sourceNote: mutant-feral archetype: hulking irradiated brute, stock post-apoc mutant type
creatures.flavor: Grew three sizes past human and forgot most of its words along the way; still remembers the name of the town it used to guard.
creatures.summary: hulking overgrown mutant brute

creatures.name: Scrap Colossus
creatures.sourceNote: scrap-beast archetype: junkyard-built walking machine, stock salvage-golem type
creatures.flavor: Welded together from three different trucks by hands that clearly loved the work; runs on spite and a leaking fuel drum.
creatures.summary: welded-together walking scrap machine

creatures.name: Chem-Baron
creatures.sourceNote: raider-warlord archetype: settlement-controlling drug/fuel kingpin
creatures.model: net-new: wasteland kingpin in scavenged finery, no bespoke model needed (uses mage stat frame only)
creatures.flavor: Runs three settlements on rationed water and homebrewed stims; smiles like he's already won the argument you haven't started.
creatures.summary: drug-and-fuel kingpin warlord

creatures.name: The Sermon-Bearer
creatures.sourceNote: bomb-cult zealot archetype: doomsday high-priest, our own invented theology (no real-world cult referenced)
creatures.model: net-new: robed zealot with a warhead-fragment icon, no bespoke model needed (uses priest stat frame only)
creatures.flavor: Preaches that the bombs were mercy and the next ones will finish the job kindly; his flock believes him, which is the scary part.
creatures.summary: doomsday high-priest awaiting the next blast

creatures.name: Ashfield Titan
creatures.sourceNote: scrap-beast archetype: settlement-sized industrial walker, stock giant-war-machine type
creatures.flavor: Built from a downed cargo hauler by a warlord who wanted a throne that could also crush things; mostly it just crushes things.
creatures.summary: hauler-built industrial war-walker

creatures.name: Glasslands Broodmother
creatures.sourceNote: mutant-feral archetype: apex irradiated matriarch, seeds a feral bloodline
creatures.flavor: Every Chittergaunt and Rustfang for fifty miles traces back to her den under the melted overpass; she remembers being smaller, and human.
creatures.summary: apex matriarch of the mutant bloodline

creatures.name: Deadman's Warlord
creatures.sourceNote: raider-warlord archetype: apex convoy-king ruling by fear and fuel scarcity
creatures.model: net-new: convoy-king in welded plate armor built from truck panels, no bespoke model needed
creatures.flavor: Crowned himself off the corpse of the last warlord and the fuel reserve underneath his throne-truck; his convoy is a moving nation.
creatures.summary: apex convoy-king, rules through fuel scarcity

creatures.name: The Last Sermon
creatures.sourceNote: bomb-cult zealot archetype: apex doomsday-prophet who holds a live warhead as scripture
creatures.flavor: Claims the final bomb is still out there, waiting for his word; nobody who's called the bluff has lived to be wrong about it.
creatures.summary: apex doomsday-prophet guarding a live warhead

creatures.name: Half-Life
creatures.sourceNote: irradiated-ghoul archetype: apex fallout-mutated horror, decades of exposure past any human baseline
creatures.flavor: Been soaking in the hot zone so long the geiger counters just give up near it; what's left of the mind is patient, and furious.
creatures.summary: apex fallout-horror, decades-deep radiation exposure

creatures.name: The Foundry Made Flesh
creatures.sourceNote: scrap-beast archetype: apex, a factory's automated defense grid fused into one rampaging mass
creatures.model: net-new: factory-fused industrial mass, no bespoke model exists yet (iron-golem stat frame)
creatures.flavor: An entire pre-collapse factory floor — presses, arms, conveyor teeth — fused by decades of slag into a single furious machine that still thinks it's making something.
creatures.summary: factory-fused apex war-machine

creatures.name: The Man in the Rubber Mask
creatures.sourceNote: stock slasher-archetype (unmasked, unnamed stalker type — no specific franchise silhouette)
creatures.flavor: He doesn't run, doesn't talk, and the mask never quite fits his face right — like it's a size too small for whatever's under it. Cuts power to the block before he starts.
creatures.summary: Silent knife-stalker in a rubber mask, cuts the power first

creatures.name: The Neighbor Who Isn't
creatures.sourceNote: body-snatcher/pod-person stock archetype (generic, no specific 50s-film IP)
creatures.flavor: Waters the lawn at 2 AM. Smiles too wide at the mailbox. Something wears the neighbor like a coat that's still learning how elbows work.
creatures.summary: A neighbor replaced, wearing the body a little wrong

creatures.name: The Homeowners' Association
creatures.sourceNote: too-perfect-family/HOA conformity archetype, original
creatures.flavor: Matching cardigans, identical lawns, a smile that's a citation waiting to happen. They vote unanimously. They vote for you next.
creatures.summary: Cul-de-sac conformity cult in matching cardigans

creatures.name: The Thing in the Storm Drain
creatures.sourceNote: under-the-street / storm-drain lurker stock archetype (deliberately not the well-known clown)
creatures.flavor: It doesn't need a face because the neighborhood kids provide the imagination for it. Rains bring it up from the culvert; the culvert never quite drains right after.
creatures.summary: Shapeless lurker that surfaces through storm drains after rain

creatures.name: The Thing Under the Bed
creatures.sourceNote: under-the-bed/closet-monster nursery archetype, original design
creatures.flavor: Only exists between the mattress and the floor, and only when the light's off. Every kid on the block has independently drawn the same picture of it.
creatures.summary: Blind floor-level lurker only real in the dark

creatures.name: Static Bride
creatures.sourceNote: the Bride/animated-corpse motif — Shelley's Frankenstein (1818, PD) & 19th-c. reanimation folklore, NOT any studio's visual design
creatures.flavor: Stitched back together from parts that never asked to be a set. Every TV on the block snows over when she walks past; she's looking for the hands that made her.
creatures.summary: Reanimated stitched-together undead bride, disrupts electronics

creatures.name: The Man Who Sold the House
creatures.sourceNote: deal-with-the-devil / crossroads-bargain motif — universal folklore + Faust legend (pre-1929 tellings, PD)
creatures.flavor: Every family on this street signed something they didn't read. He still holds the paper, and the paper is still due.
creatures.summary: Devil-bargain realtor collecting on unread contracts

creatures.name: Medusa of the Mall
creatures.sourceNote: Medusa — Greek myth (Ovid, Metamorphoses, ancient/PD); OUR setting recontext, not any film design
creatures.flavor: Works the perfume counter under fluorescent light that never shows her eyes. The food court has forty statues who lingered too long at her register.
creatures.summary: Mythic Gorgon relocated to the dead mall's cosmetics counter

creatures.name: The Kraken in the Deep End
creatures.sourceNote: the Kraken — Norse/Scandinavian sea-legend (pre-modern folklore, PD)
creatures.flavor: The community pool closed for 'renovations' in 1983 and never reopened. Something ancient and briny decided the deep end was close enough to home.
creatures.summary: Ancient sea-legend leviathan squatting in a condemned pool

creatures.name: The Toy That Loves You Back
creatures.sourceNote: cursed-toy/possessed-plaything archetype, original design (no specific doll-franchise likeness)
creatures.flavor: Batteries not included, malice included free. It waits on the shelf all day, perfectly still, counting whose room it's going to be in tonight.
creatures.summary: Possessed toy that relocates itself to your room at night

creatures.name: The Refrigerator That Remembers
creatures.sourceNote: cursed-appliance archetype, original design
creatures.flavor: Hums a little too rhythmically. Keeps things fresh that shouldn't still be recognizable. The ice maker only runs when no one's watching.
creatures.summary: Cursed kitchen appliance that preserves things unnaturally

creatures.name: The Arcade Cabinet with One More Life
creatures.sourceNote: cursed-arcade-machine archetype, original design (generic 'haunted cabinet,' no specific game IP)
creatures.flavor: High score never changes because the last kid who beat it never left the arcade. It only takes quarters, and it always has exact change waiting in the slot.
creatures.summary: Haunted arcade cabinet that keeps its high-scorer

creatures.name: The Babysitter's Watcher
creatures.sourceNote: stalker-on-the-phone-in-the-house urban-legend archetype, original (the call-is-coming-from-inside trope, generic)
creatures.flavor: He's already inside before the phone rings the second time. The kids upstairs are fine. He just wanted her to know he could've stopped that.
creatures.summary: Home-invader who calls from inside the house first

creatures.name: The Cul-de-Sac Werething
creatures.sourceNote: European werewolf/lycanthropy folk tradition (settled, non-Indigenous, widely public-domain in literary form)
creatures.flavor: Coaches Little League. Grills every Sunday. On the full moon the whole street knows to keep the dog in and not ask questions in the morning.
creatures.summary: Suburban werewolf-neighbor, folklore lycanthropy in a cul-de-sac

creatures.name: Renfield of Maple Court
creatures.sourceNote: Renfield — Stoker's Dracula (1897, PD), the servant/thrall archetype specifically, not Dracula himself
creatures.flavor: Eats bugs off the porch and swears the new guy in the house at the end of the block 'just needs some time to settle in.' He's very devoted.
creatures.summary: Thrall-servant mook, devoted to something unseen in the house

creatures.name: The Count of the Cul-de-Sac
creatures.sourceNote: Stoker's Dracula (1897, PD) — the literary vampire lord, our own suburban recontext, not any film's visual design
creatures.flavor: Bought the biggest house on the block in cash, never during daylight hours. Invites you in exactly once. That's all he needs.
creatures.summary: Stoker-lineage vampire lord who bought the biggest house in cash

creatures.name: The Skeleton in Every Closet
creatures.sourceNote: generic reanimated skeleton — folkloric/literary undead, no owner, ancient stock motif
creatures.flavor: Every house on the street has one, and every family swears it's a coincidence. It rattles the coat hangers when the furnace kicks on.
creatures.summary: Literal skeleton-in-the-closet, one per household

creatures.name: The Lawn Ornament That Turned
creatures.sourceNote: animated-yard-decor archetype (garden gnome / gargoyle-adjacent, original), stone-creature motif is ancient/uncopyrightable
creatures.flavor: Every yard has one — gnome, birdbath cherub, plastic flamingo. They hold still for the mail carrier. They don't hold still for you.
creatures.summary: Animated yard-decor ambush predator, still until you're alone

creatures.name: The Debt Collector
creatures.sourceNote: psychopomp / grim-collector folk motif (universal death-messenger tradition, settled and non-Indigenous)
creatures.flavor: Wears a windbreaker and carries a clipboard. Every house owes him something eventually — a memory, a name, a Sunday afternoon. He always collects on schedule.
creatures.summary: Folkloric collector-of-debts undead, clipboard and windbreaker

creatures.name: The PTA
creatures.sourceNote: hive-mind conformity-swarm archetype, original (mundane-turned-wrong social horror, no IP basis)
creatures.flavor: They vote as one, speak in overlapping half-sentences, and know your kid's grades before you do. Disagreement is not on the agenda.
creatures.summary: Hive-mind swarm of identical, over-informed suburban parents

creatures.name: Deep One
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Shadow over Innsmouth (1936, PD)
creatures.flavor: A shore-town's shame given gills — it wades in half-formed, croaking a hymn it hasn't earned the throat for yet.
creatures.summary: batrachian shore-dweller, croaks a half-formed hymn

creatures.name: Deep One Whip
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Shadow over Innsmouth (1936, PD)
creatures.flavor: Older, wetter, meaner — it keeps the school in line with a lashing tail and a stare that promises the tide is coming for you specifically.
creatures.summary: tide-driving enforcer of the Innsmouth shoal

creatures.name: Deep One Archpriest
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Shadow over Innsmouth (1936, PD)
creatures.flavor: It leads the chant at the reef-altar and remembers being a person before the change finished; that memory is the only mercy it has left.
creatures.summary: reef-cult elder, half-remembers being human

creatures.name: Byakhee
creatures.sourceNote: shared literary PD mythos convention (Chambers/Lovecraft-circle void-fauna)
creatures.flavor: A crow-shape wrong at every joint, it beats black wings through no air at all and only lands to feed.
creatures.summary: void-crossing carrion flock, wrong at every joint

creatures.name: Shoggoth
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, At the Mountains of Madness (1936, PD)
creatures.flavor: A slave that unmade its makers and kept the trick — a boiling black mass that grows whatever eye or mouth the moment calls for.
creatures.summary: protoplasmic slave-thing, grows eyes on demand

creatures.name: Elder Thing
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, At the Mountains of Madness (1936, PD)
creatures.flavor: Barrel-bodied and starfish-headed, it built cities on this world before anything we'd call life existed, and it still keeps better records than we do.
creatures.summary: starfish-headed elder scientist-builder

creatures.name: Elder Deep-Thing
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, At the Mountains of Madness (1936, PD)
creatures.flavor: An elder thing gone ancient and terrible, its city-building patience curdled into something that studies you the way it once studied continents.
creatures.summary: ancient elder thing, patience curdled to menace

creatures.name: Dagon
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, Dagon (1919, PD)
creatures.flavor: The father-shape the Deep Ones sing to, glimpsed once by a starving sailor and never fully described since — because no one who saw it whole stayed sane enough to try.
creatures.summary: the Deep Ones' unspeakable patriarch

creatures.name: Nightgaunt
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath (1943, PD)
creatures.flavor: Black, rubbery, and faceless, it tickles you into helplessness before it carries you off — the single most polite abduction in any bestiary.
creatures.summary: faceless black tickler that carries victims off

creatures.name: Hound of Tindalos
creatures.sourceNote: Frank Belknap Long, The Hound of Tindalos (1929, PD)
creatures.flavor: It doesn't come through space, it comes through angles — anywhere a corner exists, it's already halfway in.
creatures.summary: angle-stalking hunter that seeps through corners

creatures.name: The Colour
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Colour Out of Space (1927, PD)
creatures.model: net-new: a shifting stain of unnameable light with no fixed silhouette
creatures.flavor: Not a monster so much as a stain that thinks — a light with no name in any spectrum, patiently turning a farm, then a family, then a county into itself.
creatures.summary: unnameable light that spreads and consumes

creatures.name: Yog-Sothoth's Herald
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Dunwich Horror (1929, PD)
creatures.flavor: A half-born twin thing straining against the edges of the world it was dragged into — the Gate and the Key both wearing a body that can barely hold it.
creatures.summary: half-born twin thing straining at the seams of the world

creatures.name: Nyarlathotep, the Crawling Chaos
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, Nyarlathotep (1920, PD)
creatures.flavor: The only one of Them that bothers to wear a human face and give speeches — which somehow makes it worse, not better.
creatures.summary: the outer gods' smiling ambassador and saboteur

creatures.name: Cthulhu
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Call of Cthulhu (1928, PD)
creatures.flavor: Dead but dreaming under the drowned city that bears his name, he doesn't need to move to end you — the dreams alone have driven men to the asylum and the harbor.
creatures.summary: sunken god-thing, dreaming ruin under the waves

creatures.name: The King in Yellow
creatures.sourceNote: Robert W. Chambers, The King in Yellow (1895, PD)
creatures.flavor: He never has to lift a hand — reading the second act is enough. The tatters of his court simply keep multiplying once you've looked.
creatures.summary: the tattered monarch of a play that unmakes readers

creatures.name: Servant of the King in Yellow (Tatterling)
creatures.sourceNote: Chambers, The King in Yellow (1895, PD) — the Pallid Mask/court motif
creatures.flavor: Once someone who finished the play. Now a rag-shape in a pale mask, mouthing lines it can no longer stop repeating.
creatures.summary: pale-masked cultist unmade by the forbidden play

creatures.name: Cassilda's Mourner
creatures.sourceNote: Chambers, The King in Yellow (1895, PD) — Carcosa/Hyades imagery
creatures.model: net-new: a black-veiled wailing figure trailing tattered star-cloth
creatures.flavor: It weeps in a language that predates grief, wandering the black stars of Carcosa looking for a lake that isn't in this world anymore.
creatures.summary: Carcosan wanderer weeping in a dead tongue

creatures.name: Mi-Go
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Whisperer in Darkness (1931, PD)
creatures.flavor: Fungoid, winged, and disturbingly businesslike, it doesn't want to kill you so much as file you — in a can, for shipping.
creatures.summary: fungoid trans-void miner, files brains for transport

creatures.name: Brain in a Cylinder
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Whisperer in Darkness (1931, PD)
creatures.flavor: A voice from a metal can bolted to a speaker-horn, still insisting it volunteered for this and would love to tell you all about the stars.
creatures.summary: extracted brain, still cheerfully lecturing on the cosmos

creatures.name: Ghast of the Underworld
creatures.sourceNote: Lovecraft, The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath (1943, PD)
creatures.flavor: Kangaroo-legged and corpse-pale, it barks like a starved dog in the dark beneath the waking world and hunts in loping, delighted packs.
creatures.summary: kangaroo-legged corpse-thing that barks in the deep dark

creatures.name: The Trench Ghost
creatures.sourceNote: generic WWI-lensed infantry archetype (no named nation/unit)
creatures.flavor: A soldier who never left the line, rifle still slung, gas-hood rotted to rags; it keeps walking a patrol route that ended lifetimes ago.
creatures.summary: shell-shocked revenant infantryman on eternal patrol

creatures.name: The Legion Wall
creatures.sourceNote: classical-era shield-line legionary archetype
creatures.flavor: One tile of a wall that used to be a hundred men wide; it still steps in formation even with no one left on either flank.
creatures.summary: lone shield-and-spear legionary, drilled to a fault

creatures.name: The Musket Line
creatures.sourceNote: generic 18th/19th-c. volley-fire infantry archetype
creatures.flavor: Loads, kneels, fires, reloads — the whole drill even when there's no second rank behind him and no order left to give.
creatures.summary: standing volley-drill musketeer, drilled past reason

creatures.name: The Longship Raider
creatures.sourceNote: Norse-lensed raider archetype (not a specific saga figure)
creatures.flavor: Came ashore for plunder and glory and got neither — just the theater's endless tide instead of home.
creatures.summary: axe-and-round-shield sea raider, stranded in the war

creatures.name: The Jungle Scout
creatures.sourceNote: generic mid-century jungle-warfare scout archetype (no named conflict)
creatures.flavor: Camouflage gone to lichen, machete more rust than edge — still moves like the canopy is watching him back.
creatures.summary: camo-draped recon scout gone half-feral in the green

creatures.name: The Siege Sapper
creatures.sourceNote: medieval siege-engineer archetype
creatures.flavor: Digs toward the wall by memory, pick over one shoulder, satchel of black powder over the other, humming a tune no living ear would know.
creatures.summary: tunnel-digging siege engineer, still mining toward a wall

creatures.name: The Berserker
creatures.sourceNote: Norse saga/legend berserkr tradition (public domain; no modern media design)
creatures.flavor: Fights bare-armed and bear-shirted, past fear, past pain, past the point where the theater's rules of engagement still apply to him.
creatures.summary: battle-trance warrior who fights past fear and flesh

creatures.name: The Draugr Captain
creatures.sourceNote: Norse folklore draugr — the mound-dwelling undead warrior of the sagas
creatures.flavor: Guards a rank that was overrun centuries ago as if the order to hold still stands; corpse-cold hands still know the grip of a sword-hilt.
creatures.summary: mound-risen undead officer still holding a dead line

creatures.name: The Machine-Gun Nest
creatures.sourceNote: generic entrenched-crew-served-weapon archetype
creatures.flavor: Not one soldier but the whole emplacement fused together — tripod legs, traversing arms, a barrel where a face should be.
creatures.summary: fused gun-and-gunner emplacement, animate and traversing

creatures.name: The Storm-Trooper Cadre
creatures.sourceNote: generic elite-shock-infantry archetype (WWI stosstruppen-style, no named force)
creatures.flavor: Moves in twos and threes between the shell-holes, grenade-first, never in the open longer than a breath.
creatures.summary: grenade-and-trench-knife shock infantryman

creatures.name: The Valkyrie
creatures.sourceNote: Norse myth — chooser of the slain (public domain figure, our own visual take)
creatures.flavor: Walks the field after the guns fall quiet, marking which of the fallen the theater will keep and which it lets go home.
creatures.summary: battlefield psychopomp choosing which dead the war keeps

creatures.name: The Iron Cavalry
creatures.sourceNote: generic armored-cavalry/tank archetype, era-blurred
creatures.flavor: Half horse, half hull-plate — the theater's answer to any age's need for something that doesn't tire and doesn't feel the wire.
creatures.summary: armor-plated war-beast standing in for every era's tank

creatures.name: The Siege Tower
creatures.sourceNote: medieval siege-engine archetype
creatures.flavor: Rolls forward on its own dead momentum, ladders unfurling like wings, arrow-slits blinking where windows should be.
creatures.summary: animate siege-tower, self-propelled toward the wall

creatures.name: The Trench Wight
creatures.sourceNote: WWI-lensed mass-grave revenant archetype (not any single named ghost)
creatures.flavor: Commands a company that's mostly mud and memory now, whistle still around its neck, ready to blow the advance no one will survive.
creatures.summary: revenant trench-officer still blowing the whistle to advance

creatures.name: The War Elephant
creatures.sourceNote: ancient/classical siege-beast archetype
creatures.flavor: Armored howdah still smoking from the last volley it shrugged off; it doesn't rout, it doesn't stop, it just keeps coming through the line.
creatures.summary: armored siege-beast that shrugs off volleys and keeps coming

creatures.name: The Gorgon Standard
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — Medusa/Gorgon, invoked here as a war-banner icon rather than the individual myth figure
creatures.flavor: A standard-bearer whose face the theater blurs on purpose — look at her banner too long and you understand exactly why armies used to carry her likeness into battle.
creatures.summary: gorgon-faced standard-bearer, a banner that petrifies stares

creatures.name: The Flying Squadron
creatures.sourceNote: generic early-aviation/biplane dogfighter archetype
creatures.flavor: Half war-bird, half war-machine, strafing the line from an altitude the trenches can only pray at.
creatures.summary: aerial strafing beast standing in for the first air war

creatures.name: The Ironclad Leviathan
creatures.sourceNote: generic armored-warship archetype, era-blurred (age-of-sail through dreadnought)
creatures.flavor: It doesn't fly the theater's skies so much as displace them, guns run out along a hull too vast to have ever been launched from any yard.
creatures.summary: gargantuan warship-beast that dominates the theater's horizon

creatures.name: The War-Wyrm
creatures.sourceNote: generic siege-dragon archetype used as the theater's ultimate weapon, not tied to any named dragon myth
creatures.flavor: Chained to a war chariot bigger than most houses, it's less a monster than a munitions budget with wings and a grudge.
creatures.summary: chained siege-dragon deployed like a living artillery piece

creatures.name: The Death Knight of No Nation
creatures.sourceNote: generic black-armored undead-commander archetype (fantasy stock type, no franchise ties)
creatures.flavor: Every side in every war in this theater has, at one time, sworn he was fighting for them; he has stopped correcting anyone.
creatures.summary: undead commander claimed by every faction, loyal to none

creatures.name: The Siege of the World
creatures.sourceNote: original apex — the theater's totalizing embodiment of endless war, an original composite figure, not a myth or franchise reskin
creatures.flavor: Wears every era's uniform at once and none convincingly; the theater's honest answer to what War would look like if it ever had to show its face.
creatures.summary: war given a body, wearing every era's uniform at once

creatures.name: the Drowned Captain
creatures.sourceNote: generic mad-captain figure in the vein of Melville's Ahab (1851, PD) — our own obsessive, not Ahab himself
creatures.flavor: Lashed to a wheel that rotted out from under him decades ago, he still barks headings to a crew that stopped answering. Cross his wake and he'll press every soul aboard into one more hunt.
creatures.summary: undead ship's-master, obsessed and unable to stop commanding

creatures.name: Bosun Wormwood
creatures.sourceNote: stock cutthroat-pirate-mook archetype (uncopyrightable stock type)
creatures.flavor: Every crew needs someone to swing first and count the take later. He's not smart, he's not brave, but there's always another one behind him.
creatures.summary: rank-and-file cutlass pirate, first over the rail

creatures.name: the Bone Quartermaster
creatures.sourceNote: undead-crew archetype built on the ghost-ship stock trope
creatures.flavor: He still keeps the manifest, tallying cargo that turned to silt a hundred years back. Argue with his math and he'll settle it with a cutlass.
creatures.summary: undead crewman, ledger-obsessed and cutlass-armed

creatures.name: the Kraken
creatures.sourceNote: Norse/Scandinavian sea-monster legend, pre-modern folklore (also the Alfred Tennyson sonnet, 1830, PD)
creatures.flavor: Sailors call it a myth right up until the sea stands up around their ship. It doesn't hunt for food anymore — it hunts because something that old resents being disturbed.
creatures.summary: the mythic apex sea-titan, rarely surfaces, never forgotten

creatures.name: Moby, the White Whale
creatures.sourceNote: Melville, Moby-Dick (1851, PD) — the whale itself, not any adaptation's design
creatures.flavor: Pale as bone and scarred by a hundred failed harpoons, it doesn't flee ships — it turns and comes back for them. Some captains hunt it for the bounty. Others hunt it because they can't stop.
creatures.summary: the pale, unkillable whale that turns and fights back

creatures.name: a Siren
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — the Sirens (Homer's Odyssey, ancient/PD)
creatures.flavor: The song doesn't promise treasure or lust — it promises rest, which is worse, because half the crew actually wants that. She only has to be patient; the rocks do the rest.
creatures.summary: reef-perched singer whose song offers exhausted sailors relief

creatures.name: a Siren-Flock Screecher
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — the Sirens, junior/flock member
creatures.flavor: Not every siren has the voice for the killing song — the young ones just shriek and dive-bomb, hoping to knock a sailor loose from the rigging while their elders finish the job.
creatures.summary: young siren, screeches and dives rather than enchants

creatures.name: Scylla
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — Scylla, the six-headed strait-monster (Homer's Odyssey, ancient/PD)
creatures.flavor: She doesn't chase ships — she waits in the same strait she's waited in since before anyone's grandmother, and takes exactly one sailor from every hull that passes too close to her side.
creatures.summary: strait-bound many-headed horror, takes a toll from every passing hull

creatures.name: the Charybdis Maw
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — Charybdis, the whirlpool-monster paired with Scylla (Homer's Odyssey, ancient/PD)
creatures.flavor: Not a creature so much as an appetite the sea itself grew — three times a day the strait empties into her throat and nothing caught in the pull ever argues its way back out.
creatures.summary: living whirlpool that swallows the strait on a rhythm

creatures.name: the Flying Dutchman's Wheelman
creatures.sourceNote: the Flying Dutchman — Cape maritime legend, pre-modern folklore (first written accounts 18th c.)
creatures.flavor: Doomed to round the same cape forever, the ship's own helm has become a creature of splintered wood and drowned will — it doesn't want passengers, it wants company in the doom.
creatures.summary: the cursed ghost-ship itself, animate and hunting for crew

creatures.name: a Dutchman Deckhand
creatures.sourceNote: the Flying Dutchman legend — the doomed crew, pre-modern folklore
creatures.flavor: Soaked through and past caring, they still haul the same lines they died hauling. Boarding one ship is the same as boarding the next, to them — the work never ends.
creatures.summary: waterlogged member of the cursed eternal crew

creatures.name: Davy Jones's Chain-Ghoul
creatures.sourceNote: Davy Jones's Locker — sailors' folk-idiom for the seabed afterlife, maritime folklore (not a specific character design)
creatures.flavor: Every drowned sailor goes to the Locker eventually, the old saying goes — and some of them claw back up the anchor chain first, still hungry for one more meal above the waterline.
creatures.summary: drowned-sailor ghoul climbing up from the seabed locker

creatures.name: the Locker-Warden
creatures.sourceNote: Davy Jones's Locker folk-idiom, personified as its own keeper — our invention on the folklore, not a claimed character
creatures.flavor: Every sailor swears the Locker has a keeper who counts the dead as they settle. Whether that's true or just something sailors tell each other in a storm, something down there is definitely counting.
creatures.summary: the folkloric seabed afterlife given a keeper, vast and patient

creatures.name: a Sea Hag of the Shoals
creatures.sourceNote: folk sea-hag figure, generic maritime witch-crone (not tied to any single copyrighted work)
creatures.flavor: She trades storms for secrets and secrets for storms, and never tells you which one you actually bought. Sailors leave offerings on the reef so she'll look the other way.
creatures.summary: reef-dwelling hag who barters weather for confessions

creatures.name: a Sahuagin Raider
creatures.sourceNote: generic fish-humanoid raider archetype (own deep-water raider framing, no external IP)
creatures.flavor: They rise off the reef in packs when a hull rides too low and too slow, stripping a wreck bare before the survivors even reach the boats.
creatures.summary: reef-raiding fish-humanoid, opportunistic wreck-stripper

creatures.name: a Sahuagin Depth-Priest
creatures.sourceNote: generic fish-humanoid priest archetype, own deep-sea cult framing
creatures.flavor: He blesses the raids in a tongue that predates any surface language, and the raiders fight harder for it — not out of faith exactly, more like fear of what he'd do if they didn't.
creatures.summary: deep cult priest who blesses reef-raids with dread invocations

creatures.name: a Merrow Wrecker
creatures.sourceNote: generic ogre-of-the-sea archetype (folkloric merrow stock type, no specific IP)
creatures.flavor: Not clever, just strong and hungry and drawn to the sound of splintering hulls. A merrow doesn't wreck ships for treasure — treasure's just what's left after it eats.
creatures.summary: brutish sea-ogre that swarms wrecks for the meal, not the loot

creatures.name: the Bosun's Ghost
creatures.sourceNote: generic maritime-haunting archetype — the officer who died on duty and can't leave it
creatures.flavor: He still walks his rounds belowdecks, and any living sailor who hears his whistle in the dark knows to brace for something going badly wrong topside within the hour.
creatures.summary: haunting ship's-officer whose whistle warns (or curses) the crew

creatures.name: a Corsair Deckhand
creatures.sourceNote: generic historical-corsair mook archetype — long-dead seafaring raider figure, not any named individual
creatures.flavor: Fast over the rigging and faster with a knife, these are the ones sent ahead to cut lines and douse lanterns before the boarding party even shows itself.
creatures.summary: nimble boarding-raider, cuts lines before the main assault

creatures.name: the Storm-Bound Djinn
creatures.sourceNote: elemental sea-storm archetype drawn from the broad genie/elemental stock type of maritime legend
creatures.flavor: Bound into a waterspout centuries ago by a captain who never wrote down how, it now answers to no one and drags whole ships skyward just to watch them fall.
creatures.summary: elemental genie fused into a waterspout, capricious and huge

creatures.name: the Wrecking Reef-Wraith
creatures.sourceNote: generic ghost-of-the-shoals archetype — the drowned wrecker who lured ships onto rocks in life
creatures.flavor: In life it lit false beacon-fires to lure ships onto the rocks for salvage. In death it just lights the fires — there's no cargo left to want, only the habit.
creatures.summary: drowned wrecker's ghost, still luring ships onto the rocks

creatures.name: Medusa
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth (Perseus cycle)
creatures.flavor: A cursed priestess left to guard a ruin no one else will enter; she doesn't hunt, she waits for you to look.
creatures.summary: snake-haired gaze-petrify guardian of a forbidden shrine

creatures.name: the Minotaur
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth (Theseus / Cretan labyrinth)
creatures.flavor: Bred as a punishment and grown into a king of his own maze — the walls moved to keep him, so now he moves them to keep you.
creatures.summary: bull-headed labyrinth-warden, gores anything that gets turned around

creatures.name: the Hydra
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth (Labors of Herakles)
creatures.flavor: Every wound you land is a negotiation it wins later — cut deep enough, fast enough, or it simply outlasts you with one more mouth.
creatures.summary: regenerating many-headed swamp apex predator

creatures.name: the Cyclops
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth (Homer's Odyssey, Polyphemus)
creatures.flavor: He counts his flock by touch, one eye or none, and either way he's never once lost track of an intruder.
creatures.summary: one-eyed shepherd-giant sentry, brutal in close quarters

creatures.name: the Oracle Cyclops
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — Cyclopes as forge-kin of Hephaestus / seer tradition
creatures.flavor: Blinded on purpose, so the story goes, in trade for seeing further — he'll tell you your death before he deals it.
creatures.summary: blind seer-giant, prophetic elite variant of the sentry

creatures.name: the Chimera
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth (Iliad; Bellerophon cycle)
creatures.flavor: Three heads, three different opinions about how you should die — the goat screams first so the lion and the dragon don't have to.
creatures.summary: lion/goat/serpent composite, breathes fire mid-roar

creatures.name: the Harpy
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth (Argonautica; Aeneid)
creatures.flavor: They don't so much attack as infest — a shrieking cloud that strips a camp of food and morale in the same pass.
creatures.summary: filth-winged bird-woman raider, hunts in screaming flocks

creatures.name: the Harpy Matriarch
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — harpy tradition, elevated to a brood-leader
creatures.flavor: Older, meaner, and smart enough to use her flock as bait — she circles while they soften you up.
creatures.summary: harpy brood-leader, coordinates the swarm's dive attacks

creatures.name: the Sphinx-Warden
creatures.sourceNote: Greek/Egyptian myth (riddle-guardian tradition, Oedipus cycle)
creatures.model: net-new: lion-bodied, human-faced, feathered-winged riddler perched on a ruined threshold
creatures.flavor: She'll let you pass if you answer well — and she is in absolutely no hurry, because she has outlived every wrong answer she's ever heard.
creatures.summary: riddling lion-bodied guardian barring a sealed passage

creatures.name: Anubis's Jackal-Priest
creatures.sourceNote: Egyptian myth/religion (Anubis, funerary tradition) — treated as a masked mortal priesthood, not the god
creatures.model: net-new: jackal-masked embalmer-priest in funerary wrappings, ceremonial flail
creatures.flavor: He was a man once, before the mask stopped coming off — now he weighs every heart that walks into his tomb, including his own.
creatures.summary: jackal-masked tomb-priest, judges intruders before it fights them

creatures.name: the Mummy
creatures.sourceNote: Egyptian funerary myth/folklore (pre-1929 literary tradition, e.g. Stoker's Jewel of Seven Stars)
creatures.flavor: Wrapped, sealed, and cursed on purpose — it was meant to stay down here forever, and it resents every second you've made that not true.
creatures.summary: bandage-wrapped rot-cursed guardian of a sealed tomb

creatures.name: Gilgamesh's Shade
creatures.sourceNote: Epic of Gilgamesh (Mesopotamian, ancient/public domain)
creatures.model: net-new: a once-great king's armored shade, bull-horned crown, still swinging for immortality
creatures.flavor: He tore down Humbaba, refused his own death twice, and still lost the one fight that mattered — now he re-fights every stranger like they might be that fight.
creatures.summary: legendary king's undying shade, apex melee boss

creatures.name: Humbaba
creatures.sourceNote: Epic of Gilgamesh — forest guardian set by the gods
creatures.model: net-new: bark-skinned forest titan, roaring face of coiled intestine-like features per the epic's description
creatures.flavor: He was posted here to keep the cedar forest safe from people exactly like you, and he has never once been relieved of that duty.
creatures.summary: monstrous forest-guardian giant, terrifying roar attack

creatures.name: Grendel
creatures.sourceNote: Beowulf (Old English epic, public domain)
creatures.model: net-new: hulking marsh-born raider, iron-resistant hide, drags prey back to the fen
creatures.flavor: He doesn't want your gold and doesn't want your land — he wants the noise you make to stop, permanently.
creatures.summary: iron-immune marsh-raider, hunts camps at night

creatures.name: Grendel's Mother
creatures.sourceNote: Beowulf — the mere-wife, avenging kin
creatures.model: net-new: a mere-dwelling avenger, drags the fight underwater to fight on her terms
creatures.flavor: She only comes up out of the mere when someone's killed one of hers — and by then the math has already stopped being in your favor.
creatures.summary: underwater ambush-avenger, drags foes into her mere

creatures.name: Raptor Pack-Hunter
creatures.sourceNote: paleontological fact (dromaeosaurid dinosaur), no IP owner
creatures.model: net-new: feathered pack-hunting dromaeosaur, quick and coordinated
creatures.flavor: One alone is a nuisance; hearing three more calling back from the treeline is the actual threat.
creatures.summary: quick feathered pack-hunter, always comes in threes

creatures.name: Pteranodon Screecher
creatures.sourceNote: paleontological fact (pterosaur), no IP owner
creatures.flavor: It doesn't want a fight, it wants your lunch — but it'll take a finger to get it.
creatures.summary: cliff-nesting flying scavenger, snatches and flees

creatures.name: Allosaurus
creatures.sourceNote: paleontological fact, no IP owner
creatures.flavor: Not the biggest thing in the valley, just the fastest thing willing to test that against you.
creatures.summary: mid-sized ambush predator, fast and relentless

creatures.name: Triceratops
creatures.sourceNote: paleontological fact, no IP owner
creatures.flavor: It would honestly rather be left alone grazing the fern-flats — it just won't be told to move twice.
creatures.summary: armored horned grazer, devastating charge when cornered

creatures.name: Tyrannosaurus Rex
creatures.sourceNote: paleontological fact, no IP owner
creatures.flavor: The valley has a food chain and one name at the top of it — everything else here is just working out how to be somewhere else when it walks by.
creatures.summary: the valley's apex predator, ends most fights in one bite

creatures.name: the Bloodless Bride
creatures.sourceNote: European folk-revenant/vampire folklore (pre-literary, no single owner)
creatures.flavor: A shambling grave-bride still in her rotted wedding linens, drawn to warmth and grief in equal measure; she doesn't hunt so much as attend, over and over, a wedding that ended badly.
creatures.summary: shuffling grave-bride, drawn to warmth and mourning

creatures.name: Renfield's Kin
creatures.sourceNote: Stoker, Dracula (1897, PD) — the Renfield archetype, generalized (not the named character)
creatures.flavor: An asylum-thin thrall who traded sanity for a taste of borrowed immortality; catches flies, counts them, offers the count up like a prayer.
creatures.summary: insect-eating thrall serving something undead

creatures.name: the Carrion Wolf
creatures.sourceNote: generic European werewolf folklore (pre-literary tradition, not any specific IP)
creatures.flavor: Not yet a full were-thing — just a wolf that has fed on the wrong grave and picked up a taste, and a little too much cunning, for it.
creatures.summary: grave-fed wolf edging toward the curse

creatures.name: Fog-Walker
creatures.sourceNote: generic Gothic-horror mist/fog-hound stock creature
creatures.flavor: A pale hound-shape that only holds together inside fog; step into clear air and it's a stray dog again, confused and harmless.
creatures.summary: fog-bound phantom hound, harmless in clear air

creatures.name: the Somnambulist
creatures.sourceNote: Stevenson, Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (1886, PD) — the split-self archetype, generalized
creatures.flavor: A respectable townsperson by day; by dusk something narrower and meaner wears their face out into the streets. They remember none of it — the gloom remembers all of it.
creatures.summary: a townsperson's cruel second self, out after dark

creatures.name: Ashen Handmaiden
creatures.sourceNote: generic Gothic-manor servant-ghost stock type
creatures.flavor: Still dusting a house that burned down a century ago; she'll answer the door for guests who knocked before her own death, and mistake the party for them.
creatures.summary: loyal ghost-servant, stuck in a burned house's routine

creatures.name: Innsmouth Hollow-Kin
creatures.sourceNote: generic isolated-fishing-village/hybrid-folk stock type (not any specific IP's mythos)
creatures.flavor: A villager whose family married the tide-line one generation too many; gill-slits under a high collar, and a hunger for the shallows nobody in town will name out loud.
creatures.summary: gill-marked villager with an unspoken tide-hunger

creatures.name: the Wolf-Cursed
creatures.sourceNote: generic European werewolf/loup-garou folklore
creatures.flavor: Cursed at a crossroads or bitten in a churchyard — the story varies by village, but the moon doesn't care which version is true.
creatures.summary: the classic moon-bound curse, mid-transformation

creatures.name: the Steward of the House
creatures.sourceNote: Shelley, Frankenstein (1818, PD) — the Creature, our own take, novel-version only (articulate, wounded, not a mute brute)
creatures.flavor: Stitched together and abandoned by its maker, it reads philosophy it finds in ruined libraries and hates almost as eloquently as it grieves; cornered, it is devastating, and it knows exactly why it became this.
creatures.summary: eloquent, grieving, stitched-together giant

creatures.name: Lady of the Blood Countess's Line
creatures.sourceNote: Le Fanu, Carmilla (1872, PD)
creatures.flavor: Centuries of patient, intimate hunting have made her gentler than any predator has a right to be — she prefers a slow, doting courtship of her prey to a chase.
creatures.summary: patient, affectionate centuries-old blood-drinker

creatures.name: the Riderless Terror
creatures.sourceNote: Irving, The Legend of Sleepy Hollow (1820, PD) — the Headless Horseman
creatures.flavor: A cannonball took his head at some forgotten muster, and every autumn he rides out looking for a replacement — pumpkin, skull, or yours, he isn't particular.
creatures.summary: headless rider hunting a replacement skull, every autumn

creatures.name: the Unseen Guest
creatures.sourceNote: Wells, The Invisible Man (1897, PD) — the Griffin archetype, our own take (a chemist undone by his own formula, not a specific film design)
creatures.flavor: Bandaged only when he wants to be seen; the rest of the time you track him by breath-fog on cold glass and the footprints that appear in spilled flour.
creatures.summary: invisible chemist, tracked by breath and footprints

creatures.name: the Portrait's Truth
creatures.sourceNote: Wilde, The Picture of Dorian Gray (1890, PD)
creatures.flavor: Ageless and lovely to look at; somewhere in the house hangs the ledger of every cruelty, rotting so its owner never has to. Destroy the portrait and you destroy the deal.
creatures.summary: ageless beauty whose hidden portrait holds the rot

creatures.name: the Baba Yaga
creatures.sourceNote: Slavic folklore — Baba Yaga (settled, widely published legend figure, not a living closed tradition)
creatures.flavor: Her hut walks on chicken legs and judges visitors before she does; help without being asked and she rewards extravagantly, ask without helping and you become the next fence-post skull.
creatures.summary: chicken-legged hut-witch who judges before she helps

creatures.name: the Gorgon's Daughter
creatures.sourceNote: Greek myth — Medusa (ancient, no owner)
creatures.flavor: She keeps a garden of the men who looked, arranged by the year they made the mistake; she's stopped being angry about it and started being a curator.
creatures.summary: gaze-cursed gorgon, curating a garden of statues

creatures.name: the Opera-House Phantom
creatures.sourceNote: Leroux, The Phantom of the Opera (1910, PD)
creatures.flavor: A genius disfigured and driven underground who built a kingdom of trapdoors and misdirection beneath the stage he was never allowed to stand on; he'll kill for the right voice as readily as he'd die for it.
creatures.summary: masked genius-architect ruling from beneath the stage

creatures.name: the Impaler-Count
creatures.sourceNote: Stoker, Dracula (1897, PD) — novel version (charismatic, ancient, commanding wolves/mist, not any film's fangs-and-cape design)
creatures.flavor: Old enough to have negotiated treaties in three dead empires; he doesn't need to chase you, because he already owns the roads, the weather, and the wolves between you and the border.
creatures.summary: ancient, courtly count who owns the road home

creatures.name: the Woeful Cry
creatures.sourceNote: Irish/Scottish folklore — the banshee (settled literary/folkloric figure, generalized, treated as an omen-spirit rather than flattened into a stock ghost)
creatures.flavor: She doesn't kill; she announces. Hearing her keen at your door is the gloom's way of telling you the paperwork on your death is already filed — what you do with the notice is still yours.
creatures.summary: keening death-omen spirit; herald, not killer

creatures.name: the House That Remembers
creatures.sourceNote: generic Gothic-haunted-house stock type (the manor-as-monster trope)
creatures.flavor: Every family that ever died under this roof left a little of their worst moment behind, and the house learned to move the furniture with it; it doesn't want visitors, it wants witnesses.
creatures.summary: a haunted manor that rearranges itself to relive its dead

creatures.name: the Playing-Card Guard
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — the Queen of Hearts' card-soldiers who paint the roses red
creatures.flavor: Flat, hinged, and utterly loyal to a rank it can't read — it swings a spade-halberd edge-on so it nearly vanishes, then face-on so it looms.
creatures.summary: flat card-soldier, obeys any shouted rank

creatures.name: the Tin Soldier's Hollow Cousin
creatures.sourceNote: stock nursery-toy-come-to-life archetype (generic wind-up soldier, not any single IP's toy line)
creatures.flavor: Painted smile, key still turning in its back; it marches in whatever direction it was last wound, even off a table's edge.
creatures.summary: wind-up soldier, marches until unwound

creatures.name: the March Hare
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — the tea-party Hare, mad from too much March
creatures.model: net-new: lanky twitching hare in a waistcoat of fur, teacup always in one paw
creatures.flavor: It never stops setting the table and never stops smashing it; ours argues with the furniture between bites.
creatures.summary: tea-mad hare, hostile to clocks and cutlery

creatures.name: a Wicked Witch's Wolf
creatures.sourceNote: Grimm fairy-tale wolves (Little Red Riding Hood / the Wolf and the Seven Young Kids, PD folk tradition)
creatures.flavor: Chalk-dust still clings to its throat from swallowing a voice that wasn't its own; it talks before it bites, and the talking is the worse part.
creatures.summary: storybook wolf, mimics a soft voice before attacking

creatures.name: Geppetto's Runaway Marionette
creatures.sourceNote: Collodi, Le avventure di Pinocchio (1883, PD) — a puppet who lied its way out of its strings
creatures.flavor: Its nose is a broken hinge that keeps lengthening whenever it insists it means no harm; the strings dangling from its wrists still twitch toward a hand that isn't there.
creatures.summary: lying puppet, nose-hinge lengthens with each lie

creatures.name: the Piper's Rat
creatures.sourceNote: the Pied Piper of Hamelin legend (medieval German folk legend, PD)
creatures.flavor: It can't help following music, even music it invents by chewing on pipes; a column of them will drown a room before the tune even lands.
creatures.summary: tune-compelled rat, swarms toward any melody

creatures.name: the Mouse King's Sentry
creatures.sourceNote: Hoffmann, Nussknacker und Mausekönig (1816, PD) — the Mouse King's seven-headed court
creatures.model: net-new: scrawny multi-headed mouse-courtier in a torn paper crown
creatures.flavor: Extra heads, extra crowns, extra grudges — it snaps at whichever slight it remembers most that second.
creatures.summary: multi-headed mouse-courtier, argues with itself mid-fight

creatures.name: the Nutcracker Grenadier
creatures.sourceNote: generic wooden-soldier toy archetype (the Nutcracker's rank-and-file, not the named prince)
creatures.flavor: Jaw hinged to crack more than nuts; painted eyes track motion better than most flesh does.
creatures.summary: wooden grenadier, jaw-hinge crushing bite

creatures.name: the Cheshire Grin
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — the cat that fades to only its smile
creatures.model: net-new: striped cat dissolving into mist, grin the last visible feature
creatures.flavor: It answers every question with a worse one and vanishes exactly when a hit should land; the grin is the last thing to go, and the first thing to come back.
creatures.summary: fading cat, taunts and phases out mid-combat

creatures.name: the Winged Monkey Raider
creatures.sourceNote: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900, PD, novel version) — the Wicked Witch of the West's flying monkey soldiers, bound by the Golden Cap
creatures.flavor: It hates every second of the compulsion and takes it out on whoever's closest; free one mid-fight and it simply leaves.
creatures.summary: cap-bound flying monkey, resents its own orders

creatures.name: the Goblin Toymaker
creatures.sourceNote: stock malevolent-toymaker/goblin-tinkerer archetype drawing on Grimm-style goblin/gnome tradition (PD folk motif, not any branded IP)
creatures.model: net-new: hunched goblin tinker hung with keys, spare parts, and a whistle
creatures.flavor: Every toy it's ever sold is still listening for its whistle; it fights by recalling its merchandise, not by swinging anything itself.
creatures.summary: toy-peddling goblin, remote-commands nearby constructs

creatures.name: the Queen of Hearts
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — 'Off with their heads!'
creatures.model: net-new: imperious card-court queen, oversized ruffed gown, axe she never swings herself
creatures.flavor: She never actually swings the axe — she just declares a sentence and the room's own furniture carries it out; the tantrum is the spell.
creatures.summary: tyrant queen, commands the battlefield instead of fighting it

creatures.name: the Grimm Woodland Witch
creatures.sourceNote: Grimm fairy-tale witches (Hansel and Gretel's gingerbread-house witch; PD folk tradition, our own original description — no film likeness)
creatures.flavor: She fattens what she can't yet eat and eats what she's already fattened; the oven is a door she keeps ajar just to hear you consider it.
creatures.summary: cannibal-witch, lures and force-feeds before the kill

creatures.name: the Wicked Witch of the West
creatures.sourceNote: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900, PD novel version) — melts to water, commands wolves/crows/bees/monkeys, not any film's green-skin design
creatures.model: net-new: one-eyed witch wrapped in dust-colored robes, umbrella-staff, no green skin
creatures.flavor: Ours is a hoarder of borrowed servants, not a green face — she never fights fair and she never fights dry-eyed once the bucket comes out.
creatures.summary: beast-commanding witch, dissolves rather than dies clean

creatures.name: the Mouse King
creatures.sourceNote: Hoffmann, Nussknacker und Mausekönig (1816, PD) — the seven-crowned rival of the Nutcracker Prince
creatures.flavor: Seven heads mean seven opinions about how you should die; killing one crown just promotes the angriest survivor.
creatures.summary: seven-headed rat-king, regenerates through internal rivalry

creatures.name: the Automaton in the Wicker Man's Skin
creatures.sourceNote: scarecrow-come-to-life archetype (generic animated-guardian toybox motif, not any branded character)
creatures.flavor: Straw where a heart should sit and a painted grin that never once needed the muscles to hold it; it guards the toybox border like it remembers being told to.
creatures.summary: straw guardian-construct, patrols a fixed boundary forever

creatures.name: the Wonderland Jabberwock
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Through the Looking-Glass (1871, PD) — 'the jaws that bite, the claws that catch'
creatures.flavor: It doesn't so much attack as arrive — burbling, whiffling, eyes of flame — and the vorpal answer is always a blade someone else forged.
creatures.summary: nonsense-dragon, telegraphs doom in verse before it strikes

creatures.name: the Tin Woodman, Rusted Wrong
creatures.sourceNote: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900, PD novel version) — the woodman who traded his flesh limb by limb for tin
creatures.flavor: Somewhere under the seams is the man who kept chopping even after every piece of him was replaced; he still oils his own joints mid-fight, out of habit, not need.
creatures.summary: hollow tin giant, mourns while it swings the axe

creatures.name: the Hamelin Piper
creatures.sourceNote: the Pied Piper of Hamelin legend (medieval German folk legend, PD) — paid in rats, repaid in children
creatures.model: net-new: gaunt piper in motley, pipe always at his lips, never draws a blade
creatures.flavor: He never raises a weapon; he raises a tune, and the toybox itself gets up to dance for him, one compelled soldier at a time.
creatures.summary: compulsion piper, turns the battlefield's own mooks against it

creatures.name: the Wonderland Executioner-Court
creatures.sourceNote: Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (1865, PD) — the trial of the Knave of Hearts, the mob of cards
creatures.model: net-new: a whirling mass of card-guards rising as a single verdict
creatures.flavor: A deck's worth of guards rising as one verdict; it doesn't think, it convicts, and it convicts everyone in reach at once.
creatures.summary: card-mob swarm, group-verdict area attacks
